---
applyTo: "src/ui/webview-react/**"
---

<purpose>
React dashboard shared by the VS Code webview and the hosted browser client. The extension remains the source of truth for workflow/runtime state; local Zustand stores hold view state, drafts, and transient UI behavior. See the sibling `webview-react-*.instructions.md` files for store, hook, component, and workspace-viewer specifics.
</purpose>

<bootSequence>
- `main.tsx` must keep `./wdyr` as the first import and rehydrate persisted stores before rendering. Moving React mount ahead of rehydrate causes first-paint layout/state drift.
- `BootstrapApp.tsx` is the handshake guard. In the VS Code panel it sends `READY` and captured theme vars before lazy-importing `App`; in standalone mode it must skip that because the hosted server already owns bootstrap/theme caching.
- `types/messages.ts` is a re-export layer over `src/types/DashboardConstants.ts` and `src/types/WebviewMessageTypes.ts`. Do not create webview-only copies of message names or payload shapes.
</bootSequence>

<stateModel>
- `workflowStore` = extension-fed execution state, output timeline, history snapshots, undo metadata.
- `uiStore` = persisted layout/modal/view state.
- `editorStore` = prompt/script draft state and pending prompt-editor inserts.
- `settingsStore` = global settings plus workflow-level overrides and effective-value helpers.
- `terminalStore` = terminal session metadata only; actual xterm instances live in `terminalRegistry.ts`.
</stateModel>

<conventions>
- Use the Vite aliases (`@`, `@components`, `@hooks`, `@store`, `@utils`, `@types`, `@root/types`, `@root/utils`) instead of long relative imports.
- Normalize UI-facing workspace paths to forward-slash, workspace-relative keys. The hosted workspace viewer and navigation helpers rely on stable normalized paths even on Windows. **Paths arriving from the harness are the exception and must not be assumed normalized**: a file-operation event's `data.path` is copied verbatim from the harness's own tool call (`BaseToolBuilder`), and in a *multi-root* workspace ctrlyoke feeds the harness absolute paths (`CliIntegration.getEffectiveAbsolute()` — true whenever there is more than one root, independent of `ui.useAbsolutePathReferences`), so on Windows it arrives as `c:\dev\repo\src\foo.ts`. Single-root workspaces get relative forward-slash paths, which is why separator bugs here are invisible until someone opens a `.code-workspace` — `referenceBasename` split on `/` alone and so rendered every multi-root file chip as a full absolute path. Any helper that splits, relativizes, or shortens an event path must accept both separators.
- Workflow undo/redo aggregation must merge harness event paths with snapshot paths through `sameFilePath` semantics (separator/case normalization plus absolute-vs-relative suffix matching). When expanding an aggregated file back into the unchanged per-step protocol, send undo entries newest-step-first and redo entries oldest-step-first because the extension coordinator applies entries in received order.
- Prefer semantic Tailwind token classes from `styles/globals.css` (`bg-editor-bg`, `text-foreground`, etc.) over raw `var(--vscode-...)` in component markup.
- **Tailwind 4 is configured entirely in `styles/globals.css`** — `@theme` tokens, `@source` list, `@custom-variant`s; there is no JS config. Sharp edges: (1) the import is `source(none)`, so classes are generated only from the `@source` paths — a new top-level folder (or a file outside the webview tree, like `src/types/SchemaUiMetadata.ts`) needs its own `@source` line or its classes silently produce no CSS. (2) The scanner does not split a class glued to an interpolation: in `` `grid animate-in${x ? " foo" : ""}` `` it sees `animate-in${x`, so `animate-in` is generated only if it happens to appear unglued elsewhere — keep a space or build the list with `.join(" ")`. (3) `hover:` is redefined as plain `&:hover` because v4's default wraps it in `@media (hover: hover)`, which would hide every `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` row action on the phone-hosted dashboard; `dark:` is pinned to a `.dark` class nothing sets, so Streamdown's bundled `dark:` classes stay inert instead of following the OS. (4) The cascade is real `@layer`s now: rules in `@layer components` lose to *every* utility regardless of specificity, and unlayered rules (`.codicon`, `.markdown-text`, `.diff`) beat every utility. Opacity modifiers on `var()` tokens (`bg-editor-bg/90`) work in v4 (`color-mix()`); under v3 they generated nothing. `npm run lint` enforces v4 spellings via `tailwindcss/enforces-canonical-classname`.
- Reuse the shared select/dropdown primitives instead of re-implementing them: `CustomSelect`/`HarnessDropdown`/`SkillsSelect`/`MultiCheckboxDropdown`/`PriorContextSelect` for the selects themselves; the `.cy-select-trigger` class (closed-state box) and `.cy-dropdown-row`/`.cy-dropdown-row-selected` classes (HC hover/selection outline) for trigger and row chrome; `DropdownHiddenToggle` + `useHideableOptions` for the per-item hide feature; and `DropdownPortal` + `useDropdownPortalPosition` + `useClickOutside` for popup positioning. Recurring control shapes belong in `@layer components` in `globals.css`, not copy-pasted utility strings.
- **Everything ctrlyoke-namespaced uses `cy`** — shared classes, CSS custom properties, CustomEvent names, and the `__cy*` injected script globals. All were `fp`/`__fp` (FlightPath) until the 2026-09-13 rename, so an `fp-` in git history or an older external reference is the same name; `cy` was checked against the obvious collision, and this repo has no Cypress and no `data-cy` selectors. The set to handle carefully in any future rename is the injected globals, because they are matched **by string across separate compilation units**: `CtrlYokeWebviewProvider._getHtmlForWebview` emits `const __cyLogMessageType__` / `__cyLogLevels__` / `__cyModuleSrc__` into the `<script>` wrapper it builds, and `scripts/bootstrapScript.ts` / `scripts/moduleLoaderScript.ts` consume them through `declare const` — as does `window.__cyExpectServerRestart` (`standalone-shim.js` → `useMessageHandler.ts`). Half a rename type-checks clean and throws `ReferenceError` in the panel at runtime, so verify against built output — the free identifiers in `out/ui/webview-scripts/*.js` against the `const __cy…` lines in `out/extension.js` — never against source.
- **`cy-no-select` is the single source for non-selectable chrome** (toolbars, headers, footers, button groups, row lists) and replaces the hand-copied `select-none [-webkit-touch-callout:none]` pair. The two halves must travel together: press-and-hold is a real gesture in this UI (`SplitButton`'s collapsed menu, every `useLongPress` context menu), and without the callout suppression iOS answers that press with its own selection callout. Plain `select-none` on a text node stays correct — this class is for control surfaces.
- Guard host-specific behavior with the existing standalone helpers instead of branching on ad-hoc URL/window checks.
- `App.tsx` should stay focused on layout composition, panel geometry, and top-level modal/overlay wiring. Business state belongs in stores/hooks, with panel refs only synchronizing visual layout.
- `test/smoke/dashboardMount.test.tsx` is the only UI test that mounts the whole `App` with **nothing mocked**, and it must stay that way — every other UI test mocks the expensive hooks, which is precisely how a React #185 crash (unstable selector → infinite `useSyncExternalStore` re-render) reaches a user with `npm test` green. It renders once per representative store state because such crashes are state-gated: the cold mount passes while a run-addressed one loops. When a change adds a panel/drawer/phase the seeded states don't reach, add a scenario there rather than trusting the component-level tests.
- **The UI suite runs with `isolate: false`: every file in a worker shares one jsdom window.** Building a fresh jsdom per file cost about twice the CPU of the tests themselves, so `vitest.config.ts` turns isolation off and `test/fileIsolation.ts` restores it per file instead: it resets the module registry (so `vi.mock` and store singletons behave as before), web storage, the injected `window.__ctrlyoke*` globals, DOM prototypes, `vi.stubGlobal`/fake timers, and any `window`/`document` listener, timer or rAF that *repo source* registered. It deliberately leaves registrations made from `node_modules` alone — cached libraries such as React DOM register once per document behind a marker, and removing theirs broke input events in every later file. So a test may freely stub a prototype or global; what it must still undo itself is state outside that list. A failure that appears only in the full run and passes in isolation is almost always such a leak from an *earlier* file in the same worker. Reproduce it deterministically by running the files in the observed order in one worker (a `BaseSequencer` subclass whose `sort` follows a given list, plus `maxWorkers: 1`), then bisect the prefix.
- `HarnessUsageWindow.used`/`limit` mean different things per harness, so never branch on them being finite alone — check `unit` too. Claude and Codex encode a percentage as `used: pct, limit: 100, unit: PERCENT`; only Copilot's account quota carries real spendable counts (`unit: REQUESTS`). `getHarnessUsageDisplay` gates its `(used / limit)` fragment on the unit for exactly this reason: without it, every Claude and Codex tooltip silently gains a meaningless "(63 / 100)". The UI fixtures historically omitted `used`/`limit` entirely, so the suite does not catch this on its own.
</conventions>

<outputActivityProjection>
- **An activity slice is one streamed batch, not one logical operation**, so `mapOrderedHistoryEntriesToMessages` must pair a tool call's halves across the *whole attempt* and then re-anchor each merged event to the slice that opened it (`normalizeStructuredActivityEvents` + `normalizeCliEventsWithSource`). The harness emits `status: initiated` in one `cliOutputEventsAppended` batch and the `completed`/`toolResult` counterpart in a later one; normalizing per slice leaves every ● block painted as still running with no ⎿ output, and anchoring to the completion instead would jump each block forward to the moment it finished. Anchoring is why the normalizer exposes `sourceIndex` at all — keep `normalizeCliEvents` a thin wrapper over it so the pairing rules cannot fork.
- **Never key an activity slice by its first event.** Only tool calls carry a stable id; a bash command, a thinking delta and a text chunk do not, so any "identify the slice by `events[0]`" scheme degrades to `${type}:0` and silently collapses every such slice in an attempt into one message. That is what destroyed 1287 of 1626 events in a single run — 718 bash events rendered as 107 perpetually-"running" blocks. Slices are keyed by `${identity}:${kind}:${activity.sequence}`; only TEXT/SCRIPT deltas deliberately re-enter an existing message, to coalesce.
- **An activity supersedes the aggregate of its own identity, never of its whole target — and only CLI activities supersede at all.** `mapOrderedHistoryEntriesToMessages` and `buildOutputRows` both drop an aggregate the activities have replaced, and both must key that on `outputMessageIdentityKey` (the single source for the `target:run:attempt:phase` key). Keying it by target erased whole rows: a step's pre/end-condition script shares its target, and a script that exits without writing to stdout streams no chunk, so it has no activity of its own — its command, exit code and verdict were deleted by the AI response's activities at the same step. Status activities stay target-keyed because an `OrderedStatusHistoryEntry` has no run/attempt/phase to key on.
- **Every producer of an `OrderedCliHistoryEntry` must stamp `phase`, including the ones that have to reconstruct it.** `phase` is part of the identity the entry is looked up and merged by, so an omission is not a missing label — it files the entry under the prompt phase, where `appendLiveEntry`'s identity match lets a condition script's output *overwrite* the step's AI response. Two producers got this wrong at once: the fabricated fallback entry in `appendStreamingEventsToOutputState`, and the `CLI_WATCH_OUTPUT` handler, which is handed a bare `CliOutput` by a watcher that replays every phase's entries and must recover the phase with `getExecutionPhaseForScriptOutputSource(output.source)` exactly as the `CLI_OUTPUT` handlers do.
</outputActivityProjection>

<outputRowEstimates>
- Virtualized output rows are estimated, then measured; the gap between the two is what makes the pane jump while scrolling. `utils/outputLineMetrics.ts` is the single source for the parts of that estimate that are **measured DOM geometry** rather than calibration, and estimators must prefer it over inventing multipliers. The load-bearing fact: a ● block's height is exactly `TOOL_CALL_BLOCK_VERTICAL_CHROME + headerLines × fontSize × 1.625 + resultLines × (fontSize − 1) × 1.625` — `leading-relaxed` is set once on `TOOL_CALL_TERMINAL` and is *unitless*, so the header (base font) and the ⎿ body (`-sm`, base − 1px) resolve to different line heights. Every distinct bash/file-operation height in a profiling session lands on that grid to within 0.005px, so a residual there means the **line count** is wrong, never the line height.
- Two traps that produced most of the historical error. (1) `OUTPUT_ROW_HORIZONTAL_CHROME` (72) in `outputRows.ts` is a *calibrated prose allowance*, not padding — it also absorbs markdown block indents and proportional-glyph error. A row inside a ● block has no padding except OutputRow's `px-[var(--spacing-md)]`, so charging it 72 over-predicts wrapping badly on long file paths; use `OUTPUT_ROW_HORIZONTAL_PADDING` there. (2) A collapsible ⎿ section (`CollapsibleOutputSection`) adds whole **block** lines at the result line height: the "Show full output" toggle above the text, and the hidden-lines notice below it while collapsed. `getCollapsibleOutputChromeLineCount` is the single source for that count in the component's contract and in both estimators (`estimateBashOutputHeight`, `buildToolCallRenderPlan`); the toggle used to be an inline button on the last visible line, and charging it a whole line then was the largest single bias on bash rows, so a layout change there must move the count with it.
- Anything that changes how much text renders must move in lockstep with the estimator's width for the same text. `getCollapsedOutputMaxChars` decides what `BashOutput` actually paints, so if its `horizontalChrome` disagrees with `estimateBashOutputHeight`'s, the row measures differently than it was estimated — by construction, on every row.
- `OutputRow` wraps CLI-group rows and adds `pt-[var(--spacing-sm)]` to a group's first row and `pb-[var(--spacing-sm)] + border-b` to its last. `cli-header` and `stats` are always exactly those rows, which is the entire explanation for their long-standing +6 / +7 bias — row estimators own this via `outputRowGroupPadding`, so per-row-kind constants should not try to absorb it again.
- `useOutputVirtualization` applies a per-bucket average scale correction on top of `estimateOutputRowHeight`. It hides systematic bias but does nothing for per-row variance, so a bucket sitting at `scaleFactor ≈ 1.0` with a large `maxAbsDelta` is still a jumpy bucket. Tune against `rowEstimateOutlier` / `rowMeasurement:updated` in the perf log, not against `rowEstimateStats` averages.
- **A diff row's height is baked into the row object at `buildOutputRows` time, so `outputContentWidth` must already be measured when rows are first built.** `estimateDiffStructuredEventHeight` returns `row.diff.renderPlan.totalHeight` and ignores the `outputContentWidth` it is handed — unlike every other estimator, which recomputes — so `estimateOutputRowHeight`'s width revalidation cannot repair a plan built at the wrong width. An unmeasured pane resolves to `DEFAULT_OUTPUT_CONTENT_WIDTH` (760), roughly double a phone's, which under-counts wrapping by the same factor: measuring in a plain `useEffect` let the virtualizer measure and cache 760-sized rows before the real width landed, and produced 78-167% under-estimates sitting beside 15% ones in the same pane. Hence the `useLayoutEffect` in `OutputSection` — it is load-bearing, not a style choice.
- **Every `OutputRenderRow.key` must be unique across the whole list, and an activity slice is not an attempt.** `useOutputVirtualization` keys its measurement cache by `row.key` (`getItemKey`) and React keys the DOM by it, so two rows sharing a key each adopt the other's measured height — the pane paints large gaps, jumps while scrolling, and the measure -> `setMeasurementVersion` -> re-measure cycle can stop converging until React throws #185 and takes the whole dashboard down (an 18-step run crashed on load; a 7-step one crashed on the first scroll). The trap is that `<target>:run<n>:attempt<n>` *used* to be unique per message and silently stopped being: the chronological activity projection slices one attempt into many messages, and each slice's `activityEvents` is its own array whose `originalIndex` restarts at 0, so every slice re-emitted `:header`, `:event:0` and `:stats`. Key slice-scoped rows through `getRowKeyBase` (which namespaces by `activityKey`) and attempt-scoped rows through `getAttemptRowKeyBase`; `getOutputDiffKey`'s result needs the same slice suffix because it is both the collapse-state key and the diff's DOM anchor id. An attempt's chrome — header/prompt/command/error opening, verdict/stats and `groupEnd` closing — belongs to the attempt, so emit it on the slice that opens the attempt and the one that closes it, never per slice.
- **A row that is rendered must end up sized by its measurement, and the pending-measurement flush is the only thing that guarantees it.** `updateRowMeasurementCache` deliberately refuses to apply a measurement inside the user-scroll grace — that is what stops a reflow landing under the user's finger — and queues it instead, so anything that drops a queued value leaves an on-screen row at its *estimate* permanently: the DOM height never changes again, so no further ResizeObserver entry is coming. The symptoms are a gap above a row and the next row's opaque `bg-[var(--bg-primary)]` painting over the tail of the previous one, both surviving after scrolling stops. Two rules follow. The flush must count as "not scrolling" (`isMeasurementFlushInProgressRef`) or it re-queues into a map it is about to clear; and it must reach TanStack through `resizeItem`, not `measureElement`, because `measureElement` silently no-ops while the virtualizer believes a scroll is in flight — precisely the state the flush exists to recover from.
- **Never return a bogus measurement from `measureElement`.** Whatever it returns *is* the row's new size — TanStack hands it straight to `resizeItem`. A 0 is routinely transient (the pane collapsed to `display: none`, or the element was observed before its first layout), so return the row's existing size instead; returning the 0 collapses the row and lets its neighbours overlap it.
- **Don't paint a row's left accent with `box-shadow: inset <n>px 0 0`.** Chromium draws an inset shadow as the difference of two rects whose top, bottom and right edges coincide, and anti-aliases those coincident edges independently — so on any row whose box lands on a fractional device pixel (every virtualized row, positioned by `translateY(<measured px>)`) it leaks a faint full-width hairline of the accent color along the row's top and bottom, which reads as a thin border wrapping each event. `getStepIdentityBarStyle` in `components/output/outputStyles.ts` paints it as a `linear-gradient` background instead: transparent past the bar so there is no edge to bleed, and unlike a `border-left` it changes no box geometry, so the row keeps the content width its height estimate was computed against.
</outputRowEstimates>

<hostBoundaryGotchas>
- The dashboard runs in a **sandboxed, cross-origin iframe*cy-Events that occur outside it never reach us — including the `mouseup`/`pointerup` that ends a drag which *started* inside the panel — and there is no VS Code API to receive host-level mouse events (and pointer-capture doesn't bridge the boundary). So for any drag-style interaction, never assume you'll get the matching release: disarm the gesture on the next in-iframe signal instead — `keydown`, `blur` (focus leaving the panel), or pointer re-entry. `mouseleave` is NOT a safe teardown trigger because it also fires mid-drag when the pointer is legitimately dragged past an edge. Canonical handling: `CodeMirrorEditor.tsx` `destroyOrphanedMouseSelection` (wired to **window-level, capture-phase** `keydown`/`blur` listeners) tears down CodeMirror's orphaned `MouseSelection`, which otherwise re-pins the caret to position 0 ("stuck cursor") on every later transaction.
- When you need a DOM handler to win over CodeMirror's own key handling, attach it at the **window/document level in the capture phase**, not via `EditorView.domEventHandlers`. CodeMirror runs keydown handlers in a chain where the keymap handles bound keys (arrows, Enter, etc.) first and breaks the chain (`return true` → `preventDefault`), so an extension-level `keydown` handler never fires for exactly those keys. Capture-phase window listeners run before CodeMirror's `handleEvent` (registered in the bubble phase) sees the key at all.
- **Editor panel expansion** has two drivers and one geometry module, `utils/editorAutoExpand.ts` (event names, causes, `CENTER_PANEL_IDS`, the 60% fraction, measure/clamp/apply). (1) Typing: `CodeMirrorEditor.tsx` emits `cy-editor-overflow-change` (`{ signedOverflow, cause }`) and `App.tsx` consumes it (stable `overflowHandlerRef` pattern, listener registered once) to grow the editor panel up to 60% of the output+editor height and shrink back on delete/submit; only `doc`-cause events expand — `geometry`-cause events merely update the re-entry guards so a manual panel-drag-smaller isn't immediately undone. Gated by the `ui.autoExpandEditorWhenTyping` ctrlyoke setting (a config-service setting, not a VS Code `package.json` setting). (2) Opening the prompt-properties drawer expands to 50% (`DRAWER_EXPANSION_FRACTION`, kept at or below the typing ceiling because it doubles as a *floor* on the typing path), because the drawer covers the editor panel and a short panel shows only a sliver of it. That resize is transitioned over the drawer's own `duration-300` slide and Tailwind's default easing — via `triggerPanelAnimation({ durationMs, easing })`, which parameterizes the pre-existing `.cy-panels-animating [data-panel]` flex-grow transition — or the panel snaps to its new height before the drawer starts moving and the two read as unrelated animations. Four invariants hold this together. `editorAutoExpandPxRef` must be set to `target - basePx` *before* `setLayout`, or the panel's own `onResize` reads the resize as a manual drag and overwrites the user's persisted base height. Growth is anchored on the **measured** panel height plus the overflow, never on `basePx + accumulator` — the accumulator drifts (percentage rounding, minSize clamping, preserve-pixel-size) and an absolute target clips the first/last line behind the header/footer. While the drawer is open its expansion height is a *floor* on the typing path (`drawerExpansionRef`), or a delete-driven shrink would collapse the drawer back out of view; a manual drag clears that ref so the close no longer restores. And because a panel reports its size from `offsetHeight` through a ResizeObserver, **every frame of an animated resize reaches `onResize` and none of them is the destination** — so an animated expansion has to suppress the base-size bookkeeping for the whole transition (`expansionSettledAtRef`), and a re-toggle inside that window must read the accumulator rather than the panel.
- **iOS Safari keyboard viewport:** Safari/WebKit does not honor `interactive-widget=resizes-content`; it can both shrink/pan the VisualViewport and leave `h-dvh` sizing based on a different viewport, creating a double-compensation gap above the keyboard. The pinning logic lives in the shared `useIosVisualViewportRootStyle` hook (`hooks/useIosVisualViewportRootStyle.ts`), applied via `style={...}` on `App.tsx`'s root and, separately, on `WorkspaceViewerModal`'s root. **It must be called again on every `fixed inset-0` root that is portaled or otherwise rendered outside `App.tsx`'s own root div** — a `document`-level `focusin` elsewhere in the page does not retroactively pin an unrelated fixed tree; each root needs its own hook instance (concurrent instances are safe — see the hook's doc comment). This mirrors the established `.safe-area-spacer` local-reproduction convention for the same class of overlay (`OutputSection` fullscreen, `Modal` size="full", `WorkspaceViewerModal`). Keep it scoped to keyboard-adjusted VisualViewport state so Chrome/Firefox keep the normal `interactive-widget` path. The pin starts from a focused editable element but must stay active until the viewport returns to normal, and suppress the root `--safe-area-bottom` spacer while the keyboard is open. The working approach: while active, **lock the body out of the scroll flow** (`body { position: fixed; inset: 0; overflow: hidden }` + `html { overflow: hidden }`) and pin the fixed root at a **constant `top: 0`** with `height: visualViewport.height`. Do NOT chase the pan with `top: visualViewport.offsetTop`: on iOS `offsetTop` tracks `scrollY`, so a changing `top` reflows the root on every `scroll` event → iOS re-pans to reveal the caret → another scroll → a **runaway feedback loop** (`scrollY` climbs unbounded, the fixed root's painted position spikes ±100px = the black overlay that "scrolls over everything"). Locking the body holds `scrollY`/`offsetTop` at 0, so a constant `top: 0` covers the visible area and the constant style no longer reflows. `body { overflow: hidden }` alone is NOT enough — only `position: fixed` on the body actually stops iOS scrolling. Never use `transform`/`translate` for the offset: a transformed root becomes a containing block that traps fixed descendants and exposes body background (an earlier "black box" variant). Save and restore the body/html inline styles, and unlock on both the keyboard-close transition and hook teardown. On unlock, also reset `scrollTop` on `html`/`body`/`#root` (not just `window.scrollTo`): iOS reveals a focused input by setting an `overflow: hidden` **ancestor's `scrollTop`** (overflow-hidden does not block that, and `window.scrollTo` does not reset it). While the root is `position: fixed` that ancestor scroll is invisible, but on unlock the root returns to flow and the leftover `scrollTop` shifts it up = "stays offset after the keyboard closes." Reset once immediately and once in a `requestAnimationFrame` (the root's fixed style clears asynchronously, so the ancestor has no scroll height until flow is restored). **Arm the lock on `focusin`, not on the keyboard-adjusted `resize`** — the two are ~300ms apart, and in that window iOS runs its own scroll-the-caret-into-view pass against a still-scrollable document. The pan it establishes outlives the pin (which uses a constant `top: 0` and so cannot compensate), painting the whole root off the top of the visible area: the symptom is tapping the editor and being left with nothing but the `EditorFooter` at the top of the screen. Locking synchronously in the `focusin` handler leaves iOS nothing to scroll. Also re-assert `resetScrollContainers()` on every viewport event while locked — iOS's reveal pass is asynchronous and can fire after the lock; resetting scroll does not reflow the root, so it can't restart the feedback loop the way chasing `offsetTop` did. Debugging note: the UX snapshot serializer starts at `#root`, so `<html>`/`<body>` inline styles and `window.scroll` — where these bugs live — are never in the serialized DOM; its "Environment at capture" section (`uxSnapshot.ts` `buildCaptureEnvironmentSection`) surfaces them plus the root's computed-vs-painted geometry, which is how the ancestor-`scrollTop` offset was found (computed `top:0` but painted `rect.top=-197`).
- **CodeMirror tooltips and the mobile keyboard:** CodeMirror's default `tooltipSpace` (`windowSpace`) measures `documentElement.clientHeight` — the *layout* viewport, which keeps its full height while the iOS keyboard is up. Left alone, the completions dropdown believes it has room below the caret and renders down into the keyboard region. `keyboardTooltipSpace` (`CodeMirrorEditor.tsx`) clamps the space to the visual viewport, which is enough for CodeMirror to flip the dropdown above the caret on its own — do not hand-roll flip logic. It must be expressed in **layout-viewport coordinates** (`offsetTop` .. `offsetTop + height`, not `0` .. `height`), because tooltip positions come from `coordsAtPos` client rects; getting this wrong hides the tooltip entirely whenever iOS has panned. `view.requestMeasure()` does NOT re-run the tooltip plugin's measure request, so viewport listeners must also call `repositionTooltips(view)` or an already-open dropdown keeps its pre-keyboard placement.
- **Dev-reload reconnect** is fragile when both the browser client and the VS Code panel are open: a full `compile` + window reload far exceeds the standalone client's reconnect patience, and a fresh-page reload watchdog can race `acquireVsCodeApi()` (callable once per webview lifetime → React crashes to raw HTML if re-called). The guards are `freshPageReadySent` in `reconnectWatchdog.ts` and `window.__cyExpectServerRestart()` in `standalone-shim.js`; change reload/reconnect timing on both sides together.
</hostBoundaryGotchas>
